title: COVID-19 lockdown effect on retail foot traffic

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (with two–way fixed effects)  

Why:  
• All stores are observed both before and after the common shock (March-2020), but only stores in counties with “strict” lockdowns face the full treatment intensity.  
• DID absorbs common time shocks (e.g., national pandemic news) with period fixed effects and time-invariant store heterogeneity with unit fixed effects.  

Key identifying assumption – Parallel Trends:  
In the absence of the stricter county‐level orders, the evolution of log foot-traffic for “strict” and “minimal” counties would have been parallel. We will:  
1. Inspect pre-period coefficients in an event-study for visual/quantitative evidence.  
2. Run a placebo DID using only the pre-periods (pretending the policy happened one month earlier) to check for spurious effects.  

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################################################################
# COVID-19 lockdowns and retail foot traffic: Difference-in-Differences
# File:  experiments/exp_b/data/s01_data.csv
###############################################################################
# Required packages
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # fixed-effects regressions & DID helpers

# 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------------
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s01_data.csv")

# 2. Main DID specification ---------------------------------------------------
# Two–way FE: store (unit_id) and month (period)
did_main <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                  data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== Main DID result ===\n")
print(coeftable(did_main), digits = 4)

# 3. Dynamic event-study (pre-trend check) ------------------------------------
# Relative month: March-2020 (period==4) is time 0
df[, rel_month := period - 4]

# Event-study with February (-1) as reference month
es <- feols(y ~ i(rel_month, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
            data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== Event-study coefficients (relative to Feb-2020) ===\n")
print(etable(es, drop = "unit_id|period"), digits = 4)

# 4. Placebo DID (pretend policy at Feb-2020) ---------------------------------
df[, placebo_post := as.integer(period >= 3)]      # Feb-2020 = period 3
df[, placebo_int := treated * placebo_post]

placebo <- feols(y ~ placebo_int | unit_id + period,
                 data = df[period <= 4],   # keep only pre-real-policy months
                 cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== Placebo DID (Feb-2020) ===\n")
print(coeftable(placebo), digits = 4)

# 5. Simple heterogeneity robustness: allow group-specific trends -------------
df[, trend := period]
trend_did <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post + treated:trend | unit_id + period,
                   data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== DID with group-specific linear trends ===\n")
print(coeftable(trend_did), digits = 4)
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: The coefficient on `treat_x_post` should be negative; strict-lockdown counties experienced larger drops in foot traffic.  

Magnitude: A log point decline around –0.6 to –0.9 is plausible, corresponding to a 45–60 percent reduction relative to minimally restricted counties.  

Interpretation: COVID-19 lockdown orders substantially depressed in-store visits, with stricter local mandates exacerbating the decline. Robustness checks are expected to confirm no pre-trend violations and no placebo effect in February 2020.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=strict-lockdown counties, control=minimal-restriction counties; shock=March 2020 lockdown
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Strict-lockdown stores show significantly lower foot traffic post-lockdown
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~30% decline in foot traffic for treated stores
